findings.problem: classify_four takes [u8; 4] and returns Vec<&'static str>, allocating a heap Vec for exactly 4 known items. For a 4-element input the entire function body is a bounded transform that should use a fixed-size array or caller-owned output buffer.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to classify_four performs a heap allocation (Vec::new + grow) for 4 pointers, destroying cache locality and adding allocator contention. The function is a hot-path candidate that pays allocation cost per invocation for fixed-size work.
findings.fix: Return [Option<&'static str>; 4] or use a caller-provided &mut [Option<&'static str>; 4] output buffer. If all 4 results are always present, return [ &'static str; 4]. Eliminate the heap allocation entirely for this tiny fixed input.

findings.problem: TODO states 'use Rayon and SmallVec because it will be faster' — an unmeasured performance claim. Rayon parallel overhead (thread pool dispatch, work splitting, result aggregation) on 4 elements will be orders of magnitude slower than sequential iteration. SmallVec with a Vec fallback provides zero benefit when the function always returns Vec.
findings.failure_mode: Following the TODO would add Rayon thread-pool overhead for 4 items (likely 1000x+ slower) and add SmallVec dependency with no measurable benefit. This is folklore-driven optimization that worsens latency and increases dependency surface without evidence.
findings.fix: Remove the TODO. If performance matters, benchmark the current sequential implementation first. For 4 elements, sequential iteration with a fixed output array is optimal. Rayon is only justified for large independent pure transforms with scaling evidence (claim-traceability.md).

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist for any performance claim about classify_four. The SKILL.md requires workload, target hardware, baseline command, baseline number, new number, and regression threshold for all performance work.
findings.failure_mode: Any proposed optimization (Rayon, SmallVec, zero-copy, etc.) is pure speculation. Without a baseline there is no way to measure improvement or detect regression. The code may already be optimal for the actual workload.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark for classify_four with realistic input distributions. Measure baseline allocation count, latency, and CPU cycles before proposing any change. No performance claim without evidence (SKILL.md line 87).

findings.problem: The iterator pipeline .iter().map(...).collect() materializes an intermediate Vec. For a fixed 4-element input this is unnecessary allocation when a fixed array or in-place write is simpler and bounded.
findings.failure_mode: Heap allocation per call. On embedded or real-time systems this is unacceptable. Even in general Rust, repeated small allocations cause allocator pressure and cache pollution.
findings.fix: Use a fixed array: let mut out = [""; 4]; then assign by index, or return [Option<&'static str>; 4]. This eliminates allocation and makes the 4-element bound explicit in the type.

findings.problem: The TODO comment suggests adding Rayon and SmallVec — both are performance tools that require measured workload and resource evidence per SKILL.md line 52 and claim-traceability.md. Rayon for 4 elements violates the 'Rayon only for large independent pure transforms with scaling evidence' rule.
findings.failure_mode: A future implementer following the TODO would introduce Rayon (slower for tiny data) and SmallVec (unnecessary when returning Vec), violating the proof-slow-execute-fast principle and adding unproven complexity.
findings.fix: Remove the TODO. Replace with a note like '// For larger inputs, benchmark before considering parallelization' or delete entirely if this function operates on fixed 4-element data.
